mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1400 thousand units signals strengthening consumer confidence and economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring a specific threshold condition.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST exceeds 1400 thousand units.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) and high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) indicates an overheating economy with restrictive monetary policy, which typically causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to heightened recession risks.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0% and FEDFUNDS > 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 104), the market anticipates a supply-side shock that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate profits face headwinds from reduced output.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 104.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the core consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% annually signals persistent inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the Federal Reserve is expected to tighten policy.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annually.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a tight labor market that typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate stronger consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST > 1400) and decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 104) signals a misalignment between consumer demand and supply capacity, which typically causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to market uncertainty about economic balance.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 1400 and INDPRO < 104.

mechanism_narrative: During the post-recession recovery phase (defined by RSAFS growth > 0.5% monthly), retail sales growth typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending drives corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods during the post-recession recovery phase (RSAFS growth > 0.5% monthly).
